paragraphs.text: Gongjian (贡尖), usually rendered [tribute tip](gongjian:definition), is the middle one of the [three tips](anhua-dark:family), Anhua's loose teas that are pressed lightly into bamboo baskets. It is sorted from the leaf that falls between the tender [Tianjian](gongjian:among-three-tips) and the stalky Shengjian. That grade records how the leaf was sorted. It does not say how well the tea was made or kept. Like every Anhua tea, it starts as [heimaocha](anhua-dark:making), a raw tea of large Anhua leaf. The leaf is fixed, rolled, piled, rolled again and dried over a pine fire, then steamed soft and pressed only lightly, as the loose tips are.

The leaf comes from [Anhua](anhua:where-it-is), a mountain county in north-central Hunan. It lies on the Zi river at the northern foot of the Xuefeng mountains, in hill country where rice is hard to grow and tea does well. The county has been called the main home of [dark tea](dark:definition) in China, and from the Ming on its tea travelled north and north-west along the [old tea roads](anhua:history), as far as Russia.

This basket was made in 2024. [Anhua tea](anhua-dark:ageing) is kept for years and is said to improve as it is kept, but no agreed number of years marks it as aged. At two years it is near the start of that keeping.

brewing.text: In a small pot or gaiwan, use water at the boil and start with a steep of about 15 to 30 seconds, a little longer each round. Pressed and aged Anhua tea is also commonly simmered in a pot.

notice.text: Pine smoke or pine resin above all, a sweet taste and aftertaste, and a mellow, thick, smooth cup; a liquor from yellow and orange to orange-red. Young tea is often smokier in the first infusions and a little bitter, sweetening as the infusions go on.
